items.title: Karyopharm files for bankruptcy, looks to merger with Ayrmid for life raft
items.snippet: Debtor-in-process financing up to $55 million could keep the lights on at Karyopharm Therapeutics for its multiple myeloma and myelofibrosis programs as the biotech waits to see if its union with Ayrmid will go through.

items.title: FDA peptide policy risks undermining drug development and patient safety
items.snippet: By allowing compounding pharmacies to produce certain unapproved peptides, the Department of Health and Human Services could, in the short term, put patients in harm’s way. Longer term, the policy shift threatens the industry that brings new medicines to market.

items.title: Sun Pharma stops eye-care drug production at Indian plant amid quality issues
items.snippet: The cessation of manufacturing activities follows a Sun Pharma recall and reports that regulators found fault with the company’s quality system.

items.title: Tiziana touts multiple sclerosis win at lower dose as high dose misses mark
items.snippet: In a mid-stage trial, the lower dose of Tiziana’s intranasal monoclonal antibody reduced microglial activation in a specific type of multiple sclerosis. But the path forward remains unclear after the higher dose failed to deliver the same benefit.

items.title: Vistagen cuts workforce for second time in 2026
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Cell therapy investment grows as safety events rankle Big Pharma's CAR T autoimmune push
items.snippet: Sail Biomedicine’s $925 million deal with Johnson & Johnson helped boost the cell and gene therapy sector over biologics in terms of venture capital fundraising in the third quarter.

items.title: U.S. bioscience jobs up 7% from 2021 to 2025: Report
items.snippet: Bioscience employment rose in 41 states, though not in California, according to a new report from the Biotechnology Innovation Organization and the Council of State Bioscience Associations.

items.title: UniQure snags May Day decision date for Huntington’s gene therapy after arduous year
items.snippet: After a year of controversial regulatory reversals, the FDA has accepted uniQure’s application for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec for priority review, with a May 1 action date. If approved, the therapy—also called AMT-130—would be the first disease-modifying treatment for Huntington’s disease.

items.title: Significant stock movers of October: Biohaven climbs, ArriVent dives
items.snippet: A fresh FDA review for Biohaven’s embattled ataxia drug lifted the biotech's shares, while a late-stage lung cancer miss battered ArriVent, which failed to rebound even after encouraging early ADC data.

items.title: Drugmakers rush to pair up with Summit’s ivonescimab ahead of key verdict
items.snippet: With companies including AstraZeneca, Pfizer and Revolution Medicines clamoring to get in on Summit Therapeutics’ Akeso-partnered PD-1xVEGF antibody, one analyst calls the asset “the next major backbone” of cancer treatment.

items.title: Plug-and-play gene therapy: FDA executes on vision that’s been in the works for years
items.snippet: Former biologics boss Peter Marks had a vision. With the FDA’s latest draft guidance, it’s coming to fruition. Speaking with BioSpace, current CBER leader Karim Mikhail said the “adapted pathway” is designed to develop personalized gene therapies more quickly.

items.title: Can Saudi Arabia's burgeoning biotech hub withstand geopolitical pressures?
items.snippet: Saudi Arabia is building the regulatory framework, partnerships infrastructure and IP landscape needed to support a biotech ecosystem, despite regional political instability. Whether it can produce sustainable biotech companies and a resilient manufacturing base for global production remains an open question, but the...

items.title: BridgeBio gears up for rare muscular dystrophy launch with FDA approval in sight
items.snippet: If approved, BridgeBio Pharma’s BBP-418—which, according to one Jefferies analyst, boasts “pretty darn compelling” data—would be the first therapy for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The FDA has an action date of Nov. 27.

items.title: AbbVie’s Q3 beat should keep ‘train rolling’ as company eyes bolt-on deals
items.snippet: Strong immunology and neuroscience sales fueled AbbVie’s latest quarterly beat as the pharma’s stock continues to hit all-time highs.

items.title: AstraZeneca employs $1.5B cost savings to reinvest back into growth
items.snippet: “You don't spend one and a half billion dollars without creating jobs,” AstraZeneca CEO Pascal Soriot said as the pharma announced a new cost savings program alongside third quarter earnings.

items.title: Regeneron achieves ‘clean sweep’ in Q3 with myriad pipeline catalysts on deck
items.snippet: Regeneron executives struck an upbeat tone on an investor call Friday as the biotech posted a consensus-beating $5.1 billion in third quarter earnings and CEO Leonard Schleifer touted the company’s ‘disease agnostic’ pipeline and approach to business development.

items.title: Sanofi targets late-phase and commercial M&A to offset looming Dupixent decline
items.snippet: Focused on ensuring growth beyond Dupixent, Sanofi wants to acquire derisked assets that may benefit from the French pharma’s commercial capabilities, executives said on Friday as they reported third-quarter earnings.

items.title: Acumen scraps sole asset after Alzheimer’s fail, plunging stock 80%
items.snippet: Acumen will implement cash-saving strategies and assess its options after sabirnetug failed to beat placebo, leaving the biotech without a clinical program.

items.title: ‘We need to do better,’ Alnylam CEO admits, as uncertainty looms over transthyretin franchise
items.snippet: Alnylam shares dropped by a quarter on Thursday, with analysts suggesting the decline puts the RNAi specialist within range for a takeout.

items.title: Once undruggable, the Wnt/B-catenin pathway shows increasing promise
items.snippet: Early-stage clinical data from our company and others point to the Wnt/β-catenin pathway as a new avenue for targeting multiple cancer types.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
